title: A spectral space is a directed inverse limit of finite sober spaces
statement: Let $X$ be a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space]. Then there are a directed set $I$ (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), finite topological spaces $X_i$ ($i\in I$) which are sober (every irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point), continuous maps $f_{ii'}:X_{i'}\to X_i$ for $i\le i'$ with $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ii'}\circ f_{i'i''}=f_{ii''}$ for $i\le i'\le i''$, and continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$ with $f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$ for $i\le i'$, such that $(X,(p_i)_i)$ is a limit of the system $(X_i,f_{ii'})$ in the category of topological spaces: the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection of $X$ onto $\{(x_i)\in\prod_iX_i: f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i\text{ for }i\le i'\}$, and the topology of $X$ is the coarsest topology for which all $p_i$ are continuous. (This is the 'only if' half of Stacks 09XX; the converse is Topology Lemma 09XV.)

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 09XX (label lemma-spectral-inverse-limit-finite-sober-spaces, line 4704), direction 'spectral implies limit', with its proof (via Lemma Tag 09XW (lemma-spectral-closed-in-product-two-point-space), embedding X into a product of two-point Sierpinski spaces, and the images X_J in the finite subproducts; 'detail omitted' twice in Stacks)
